slices.focus: Summer bridge proposal rejected; redesigned as contractor-backed voluntary boot camp for underprepared entrants
slices.summary: Derek tries to push one step further by building a summer bridge evening for incoming apprentices with no shop comfort, but hits an institutional ceiling. Veteran instructors (especially Ron Belski) frame it as lowering standards and expecting unpaid extra time, while board members worry about rigor. Derek shrinks the idea into a smaller, voluntary pre-apprenticeship boot camp with contractor sponsorship, using 'readiness' language rather than 'deficiency.' He treats the reduced version as a pilot rather than a compromise, planning to collect attendance, confidence, and early-safety data to prove the concept.
open_loops: Writing a one-page boot camp proposal with readiness framing and explicit boundaries
Securing contractor sponsorship to shift cost off JATC
Designing simple measures (attendance, early mistakes, confidence indicators)
Building a handoff sheet to identify transportation, tool, and confidence needs
Collecting data to prove the concept for a future expanded version
